acceptanceCriteria: The test's timeout is a hang detector that does not expire on a loaded but progressing host.
body: internal/observations/observations_test.go:442 starts 24 copies of the test binary under one context.WithTimeout(t.Context(), 10*time.Second). On a host at load 200 or more (12 CPUs), process start and the barrier wait alone can exceed 10 seconds, so the context kills helpers and the test fails although Append serialization is correct. Seen 2026-09-27 in a local run for the V1-0293 fix: the test failed after 12.26s with observations_test.go:463 context deadline exceeded, raised by command.Start while the helpers were still being started. Fix: derive the bound from t.Deadline() (or use a much larger fixed bound as a hang detector), and keep the serialization assertion unchanged.
title: TestAppendSerializesConcurrentProcesses fails under host load: 24 helper processes share a 10-second context
